text.p: Italy's debt market closed easier but had good support at lower levels and traders said that for now the underlying positive sentiment which has boosted Btps to recent highs still remained intact.
The September Btp Liffe contract, which ended 30 basis points down at 136.26 after a session's 136.51-135.95 range was well supported at the 136.00 level, traders said.

"A close above 136.00 is important," one said. "With Bunds up again in the 102.80 area and the Btp above 136.40 then there will be every reasonable hope of seeing the Btp again touching new highs on Friday."

"Profit-taking on the Btp is no bad thing at these levels. If it breaches 136.00 it could fall to 135.50/80 but this still wouldn't change the target of 137.00," one trader said. "Only if it fell further would this indicate an inversion of the trend."
"Today there was a bit more volatility than in past days and we were affected by the dollar's strong fall and the weakness of other markets," another said.

The dollar eased as the mark firmed after the Bundesbank sought to brake the dollar's recent surge against the mark. Buba president Tietmeyer also said there was more to EMU than just the deficit criterion, like debt levels, Italian traders noted.

"We could see their was a bit of tension today. In fact on any piece of news players were trying to pull the market down so they could get back in at lower prices," said one trader referring to Tietmeyer's comments on the dollar and EMU.
On the cash market, the February 2007 Btp lost 22 basis points to 102.35, yielding 6.51 percent. The Btp/Bund spread was steady around 94/95 bps.
